source_target_content: Achieve an annual production of sustainable biomethane of 35 billion cubic meters by 2030
impact_target_content: 1.a Legally protect a minimum of 30% of the EU’s land area
justification: The production of sustainable biomethane requires large areas of land for feedstock production, which could lead to land-use changes and potentially conflict with the goal of protecting 30% of the EU's land area.

source_target_content: Each Member State shall set an obligation on fuel suppliers to ensure that: (B) the combined share of advanced biofuels and biogas produced from the feedstock listed in Part A of Annex IX and of renewable fuels of non-biological origin in the energy supplied to the transport sector is at least 1% in 2025 and 5.5% in 2030, of which a share of at least 1 percentage point is from renewable fuels of non-biological origin in 2030. Directive (EU) 2023/2413
impact_target_content: 2.a Strictly protect at least a third of the EU'S protected areas
justification: The use of advanced biofuels and renewable fuels of non-biological origin could lead to an increased demand for biomass, potentially threatening protected areas and their biodiversity.

source_target_content: The share of biofuels and biogas produced from the feedstock listed in Part B of Annex IX in the energy content of fuels and electricity supplied to the transport sector shall, except in Cyprus and Malta, be limited to 1.7%. Directive (EU) 2023/2413
impact_target_content: 5. The decline of pollinators is reversed
justification: The limitation on biofuels produced from certain feedstocks could help reduce the pressure on pollinators and their habitats, thus supporting the reversal of their decline.

source_target_content: Aviation fuel suppliers shall also ensure that Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) made available to aircraft operators at each Union airport will be at least 2% from 2025, 6% from 2030, 20% from 2035, 34% from 2040, 42% from 2045 and 70% from 2050. Regulation (EU) 2023/2405
impact_target_content: Terrestrial, coastal and freshwater ecosystems. Member States shall put in place the restoration measures for the terrestrial, coastal and freshwater habitats of the species listed in Annexes II, IV and V
justification: The production of SAF could lead to an increased demand for biomass, potentially supporting the restoration of degraded ecosystems and habitats.

source_target_content: The yearly quantity of aviation fuel uplifted by a given aircraft operator at a given Union airport shall be at least 90% of the yearly aviation fuel required, to avoid tankering practices which would bring additional emissions from extra weight. Regulation (EU) 2023/2405
impact_target_content: (pollinator) Member States shall, by putting in place in a timely manner appropriate and effective measures, improve pollinator diversity and reverse the decline of pollinator populations
justification: The reduction of tankering practices could lead to a decrease in energy consumption and emissions, potentially supporting the improvement of pollinator diversity and the reversal of their decline.

source_target_content: States shall ensure that, at all airports of the TEN-T core network and TEN-T comprehensive network, the provision of electricity supply to stationary aircraft is ensured by 31 December 2029, at all aircraft remote stands used for commercial air transport operations to embark or disembark passengers or to load or unload goods Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: 1.b Legally protect a minimum of 30% of the EU's sea area
justification: The provision of electricity supply to airports could support the protection of marine ecosystems and habitats, potentially contributing to the protection of 30% of the EU's sea area.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that at least one installation providing shore-side electricity supply to inland waterway vessels is deployed at all TEN-T core inland waterway ports by 1 January 2025, at least one installation providing shore-side electricity supply to inland waterway vessels is deployed at all TEN-T comprehensive inland waterway ports by 1 January 2030. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: In accordance with the CFP, it is crucial to continue and accelerate the work of rebuilding and keeping fish stocks above MSY levels
justification: The deployment of shore-side electricity supply installations could support the protection of aquatic ecosystems and the rebuilding of fish stocks.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that a minimum shore-side electricity supply for seagoing container ships and seagoing passenger ships is provided in TEN-T maritime ports. To that end, by 31 December 2029 TEN-T core and comprehensive maritime ports [...] are equipped to provide each year shore-side electricity supply for at least 90 % of the total number of port calls of seagoing container ships above 5.000 gross tonnes that are moored at the quayside at the maritime port concerned and 90% of the total number of port calls of seagoing ro-ro passenger ships above 5.000 gross tonnes and seagoing high-speed passenger craft above 5.000 gross tonnes that are moored at the quayside at the maritime port concerned Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: Terrestrial, coastal and freshwater ecosystems. Member States shall ensure that condition is known for at least 90% of the area distributed overall habitat types listed in Annex I by 2030 and 100% by 2040.
justification: The provision of shore-side electricity supply could support the protection of marine ecosystems and habitats, potentially contributing to the knowledge of the condition of terrestrial, coastal, and freshwater ecosystems.

source_target_content: EU fisheries are encouraged to continue the positive trend, as observed for the period 2009-2019, towards reducing fuel intensity by reducing the fossil-fuel consumption per kg of landed product for at least an additional 15% for the period 2019-2030. Energy Transition of the EU Fisheries and Aquaculture sector
impact_target_content: 13. The losses of nutrients from fertilisers are reduced by 50%, resulting in the reduction of the use of fertilisers by at least 20%
justification: The reduction of fuel intensity in the fisheries sector could lead to a decrease in the use of fertilizers, supporting the reduction of nutrient losses.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that, at the end of each year, the following power output targets are met cumulatively: (a) for each light-duty battery electric vehicle registered in their territory, a total power output of at least 1.3 kW is provided through publicly accessible recharging stations, and (b) for each light-duty plug-in hybrid vehicle registered in their territory, a total power output of at least 0.80 kW is provided through publicly accessible recharging stations. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: (agricultural ecosystems) Member States shall put in place measures which shall aim to restore organic soils in agricultural use constituting drained peatlands.
justification: The deployment of publicly accessible recharging stations could support the protection of organic soils and the restoration of drained peatlands, potentially contributing to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that along the TEN-T core and comprehensive network, publicly accessible recharging pools dedicated to light-duty vehicles deployed in each direction of travel with a maximum distance of 60 km in-between them offering a power output of at least 600kW and including at least one recharging point with an individual power output of at least 150 kW. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: Reach no net land take
justification: The deployment of recharging pools could support the protection of natural habitats and ecosystems, potentially contributing to the goal of reaching no net land take.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2030 (with intermediate 2025 and 2027 targets), along the TEN-T core road network, publicly accessible recharging pools dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles are deployed in each direction of travel with a maximum distance of 60 km between them [...]. Along the TEN-T comprehensive road network, recharging pools dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles are deployed in each direction of travel with a maximum distance of 100 km between them and each recharging pool offers a power output of at least 1.500 kW and includes at least one recharging point with an individual power output of at least 350 kW. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: Terrestrial, coastal and freshwater ecosystems. Member States shall put in place the restoration measures [...] to improve to good condition areas of habitat types listed in Annex I which are not in good condition.
justification: The deployment of recharging pools for heavy-duty electric vehicles could support the restoration of degraded ecosystems and habitats, potentially contributing to the improvement of their condition.

source_target_content: By 31 December 2030, in each safe and secure parking area at least four publicly accessible recharging stations dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles with an individual power output of at least 100 kW are deployed. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: (agricultural ecosystems) Member States shall put in place measures which shall aim to achieve an increasing trend at national level of at least two out of the three following indicators in agricultural ecosystems
justification: The deployment of recharging stations for heavy-duty electric vehicles could support the protection of agricultural ecosystems, potentially contributing to the achievement of an increasing trend in at least two of the three indicators.

source_target_content: By 31 December 2030, in each urban node publicly accessible recharging points dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles with an aggregated power output of at least 1 800 kW are deployed, provided by recharging stations with an individual power output of at least 150 kW. Regulation (EU) 2023/180
impact_target_content: 11. At least 25.000 km of free-flowing rivers are restored
justification: The deployment of recharging points for heavy-duty electric vehicles in urban nodes could support the protection of aquatic ecosystems, potentially contributing to the restoration of free-flowing rivers.

source_target_content: The average CO2 emissions of the Union fleet of new heavy-duty motor vehicles [...], off-road vehicles and off-road special purpose vehicles shall be reduced by the following percentages compared to the average CO2 emissions of the reporting period of the year 2019: (a) 15% for vehicle sub-groups 4-UD, 4-RD, 4-LH, 5-RD, 5-LH, 9-RD, 9-LH, 10-RD and 10-LH for the reporting periods of the years 2025 to 2029, (b) 45% for all vehicle sub-groups other than vocational vehicles for the reporting periods of the years 2030 to 2034, (c) 65% for all vehicle sub-groups for the reporting periods of the years 2035 to 2039, (d) 90% for all vehicle sub-groups for the reporting periods of the year 2040 onwards Regulation (EU) 2024/1610
impact_target_content: 6. The risk and use of chemical pesticides is reduced by 50%, and the use of more hazardous pesticides is reduced by 50%
justification: The reduction of CO2 emissions from heavy-duty vehicles could lead to a decrease in the use of chemical pesticides, supporting the reduction of their risk and use.

source_target_content: The yearly average GHG intensity of the energy used on board by a ship during a reporting period shall be reduced, compared to the reference value (91.16 gCO2e/MJ) by: 2% from 1 January 2025, 6% from 1 January 2030, 14.5% from 1 January 2035, 31% from 1 January 2040, 62% from 1 January 2045, 80% from 1 January 2050. Regulation (EU) 2023/1805
impact_target_content: Terrestrial ecosystems. Member States shall put in place [...] measures [...] to jointly cover, as a Union target, throughout the areas and ecosystems [...] defined in Art. 2, by 2030, at least 20% of land areas in need of restoration and, by 2050, all ecosystems in need of restoration.
justification: The reduction of GHG intensity of ship fuels could support the restoration of degraded ecosystems and habitats, potentially contributing to the achievement of the target of restoring at least 20% of land areas in need of restoration by 2030.

source_target_content: Cut the emissions of transport sector by 90% by 2050 relative to 1990. Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy
impact_target_content: Marine ecosystems. Member States shall put in place [...] measures [...] to jointly cover, as a Union target, throughout the areas and ecosystems [...] defined in Art. 2, by 2030, at least 20% of sea areas in need of restoration and, by 2050, all ecosystems in need of restoration.
justification: The reduction of transport emissions could support the protection of marine ecosystems, potentially contributing to the restoration of at least 20% of sea areas in need of restoration by 2030.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2030, at least one publicly accessible hydrogen refuelling station is deployed in each urban node. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: Marine ecosystems. Member States shall put in place the restoration measures [...] to improve [...] areas of habitat types listed in Annex II which are not in good condition.
justification: The deployment of hydrogen refuelling stations could support the protection of marine ecosystems, potentially contributing to the restoration of degraded habitats.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2030, publicly accessible hydrogen refuelling stations with a total capacity of at least 1 tonne per day, and equipped with at least a 700 bar dispenser, are deployed at least every 200 km along the TEN-T (Trans-European Transport Network) core network Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: ecosystems. Member States shall put in place the restoration measures that are necessary to re-establish the habitat types of groups 1-6 listed in Annex II
justification: The deployment of hydrogen refuelling stations along the TEN-T core network could support the restoration of ecosystems, potentially contributing to the re-establishment of habitat types.

source_target_content: For [...] ‚Äúurban buses‚Äù manufacturers shall comply with the 90% (in the reporting period 2030-2034) and 100% (as from 2035) minimum shares in their fleet of new heavy-duty vehicles Regulation (EU) 2024/1610
impact_target_content: 2b. Strictly protect all remaining EU primary and old- growth forests
justification: The increase in the use of urban buses could lead to an increased demand for biomass, potentially threatening primary and old-growth forests.

source_target_content: Member States with maritime ports shall endeavour to ensure that as of 2030 the share of renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBOs) in the total amount of energy supplied to the maritime transport sector is at least 1.2%. Directive (EU) 2023/2413
impact_target_content: 14. Cities with at least 20.000 inhabitants have an ambitious Urban Greening Plan
justification: The increase in the use of RFNBOs in maritime transport could support the protection of urban ecosystems, potentially contributing to the achievement of ambitious Urban Greening Plans.

source_target_content: Of the SAF targets reported above, synthetic aviation fuels should represent a minimum share of 1.2% from 2030, 5% from 2035, 10% from 2034, 15% from 2045, and 35% from 2050. Regulation (EU) 2023/2405
impact_target_content: (urban ecosystems) By 2030, Member States shall ensure that there is no net loss in the total national area of urban green space, and of urban tree canopy cover in urban ecosystem areas.
justification: The increase in the use of synthetic aviation fuels could support the protection of urban ecosystems, potentially contributing to the achievement of no net loss in urban green space and tree canopy cover.

source_target_content: In the first phase, from 2020 up to 2024, the strategic objective is to install at least 6 GW of renewable hydrogen electrolysers in the EU. In the second phase, from 2025 up to 2030, the strategic objective is to install at least 40 GW of renewable hydrogen electrolysers. A Hydrogen Strategy for a climate-neutral Europe
impact_target_content: (trees) When identifying and implementing the restoration measures to meet the objectives and obligations set out in Articles 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, Member States shall aim to contribute to the commitment of planting at least three billion additional trees by 2030
justification: The production of renewable hydrogen could support the protection of forests and the achievement of the target of planting at least three billion additional trees by 2030.

source_target_content: Reduce the average door-to-door cost of combined transport operations by at least 10% within 7 years Proposal for a Directive to support framework for intermodal transport of goods
impact_target_content: (forest ecosystems) Member States shall achieve an increasing trend at national level of at least six out of seven of the following indicators in forest ecosystems
justification: The reduction of transport costs could support the protection of forest ecosystems, potentially contributing to the achievement of an increasing trend in at least six of the seven indicators.

source_target_content: Zero-emission in urban logistics The new EU Urban Mobility Framework.
impact_target_content: (forest ecosystems) Member States shall achieve an increasing trend at national level of the common forest bird index
justification: The promotion of zero-emission urban logistics could support the protection of forest ecosystems, potentially contributing to the achievement of an increasing trend in the common forest bird index.
